purpose: Measure whether combining the existing arms beats the best single arm on the shared decision contract, and at what latency cost.

group_split.note: Split by group_key_for so near-duplicates cannot straddle; only needed for parameter-fitting variants, none of which are ranked above.

limitations: ML-only binary detection on one 4000-row battery; rules, semantic veto and product gating are excluded. These are not product recall/FPR.

No configuration here fits a parameter, so the full battery is a legitimate readout, but SELECTING the winner over ~30 configurations on these rows is itself a choice made on this data. Confirm any pick on a fresh battery before shipping it.
An ensemble runs every member: latency is the sum, and the deployed runtime currently loads exactly one ONNX model, so multi-member configurations are not drop-in.
McNemar p-values are exploratory: rows within a source family are correlated, and the values are unadjusted for multiple comparisons.
